intro: Each workflow reads the semi-synthetic line list from this repository, at a fixed commit. Start from an empty canvas: Project, then New project.

workflows.name: How did the outbreak unfold, month by month?

steps.label: Subject
steps.value: A semi-synthetic measles line list made safe to teach with

steps.label: This workflow’s name — the question it answers
steps.value: How did the outbreak unfold, month by month?

steps.note: 2,606 suspected measles cases notified in Sierra Leone, one row each. The file is semi-synthetic: whole records were swapped between cases of the same district and month, and every date moved by up to a week and set to its Monday. The curve keeps its shape; no row is a real person.

steps.label: URL of a CSV, Stata file or zip
Columns to keep, pasted or typed
steps.value: Case number, Organisation unit name, Residential District, Sex, Onset/Start date, Date seen at Health Facility/Community, LRS Specimen test 01 - result

steps.label: Unit of the value (entered by you)

steps.note: Keep the cases whose onset falls in 2019 to 2023. Two onsets fall outside the visits’ span, in 2017 and 2025, and 389 cases have no onset at all. The step leaves them out and says how many: they are findings about the file, not cleaned away.
A line list has no count in it, so count its rows by the onset date.

steps.label: Records arrive as
steps.shown: a table, each row a count

steps.note: Five years is about 260 weeks, more than a chart here draws; count by month, as multi-year measles surveillance is usually shown. Every date in the file was set to a Monday, so a week starting Monday is the finer choice for one year.

steps.label: Chart title
steps.value: Suspected measles cases by month of onset, Sierra Leone, 2019 to 2023

steps.label: Subtitle / context
steps.value: Every notified suspected case with an onset date in 2019 to 2023. Semi-synthetic: each date moved by up to a week, so a case near a month boundary may sit in the next.

steps.label: Source / method note
steps.value: Sierra Leone FETP line list, de-identified and made semi-synthetic for teaching (example-2019-sierra-leone-measles). Suspected cases, not confirmed ones.

steps.see: the curve rising through 2022 and peaking in 2023

steps.label: This workflow’s name — the question it answers

steps.note: Each case names the facility it was seen at, under Organisation unit name. The file has no coordinates: the facilities are found by name in GRID3’s register of Sierra Leone’s health facilities (CC BY 4.0).

steps.label: URL of a CSV, Stata file or zip
Columns to keep, pasted or typed
steps.value: Case number, Organisation unit name, Residential District, Sex, Onset/Start date, Date seen at Health Facility/Community, LRS Specimen test 01 - result

steps.label: Unit of the value (entered by you)

steps.note: Count the cases at each facility, keeping its district, which tells apart two facilities of one name.

Band each facility by its count. This file’s terms ask that a facility be mapped only where its count is large enough not to point at one child, so the band is also what decides which facilities are shown.
Keep the facilities with ten cases or more. The rest are counted, not mapped.

steps.label: Values to keep, one per line

steps.note: Show the facilities kept, in the table, and run: the next step reads their columns from it.
A name ending in Communities is a chiefdom’s community reporting, an area rather than a facility: it has no point, and is counted.
Fetch the register once; it is kept on this device, and the run makes no request.
The map places each facility against Sierra Leone’s outline, published by geoBoundaries.
Colour each facility by its band.

steps.label: Pin class for Find health facilities

steps.see: every facility name marked: matched exactly, allowing for spelling, a type that differs, ambiguous, an area, or not found
the facilities with ten cases or more, coloured by band, its key naming each

steps.note: A count by district mostly shows where people live. Divided by each district’s population, it says where a case was most frequent for the people living there.
